title: Define “first production launch” (Hosted API) + minimum checklist steps
creator: Nikhil Sharma
project: Guided onboarding + first production launch checklist
description:
Goal
Define (1) what counts as a customer’s “first production launch” for the Hosted API and (2) the minimum, unambiguous checklist steps that we can confidently recommend to self-serve developers as the baseline for going live.

Why this matters
- We’re adding an in-product checklist; without a tight definition of “production,” the checklist becomes either too vague (“add monitoring”) or too heavy (enterprise-grade readiness).
- We need a definition that is (a) measurable via onboarding telemetry for funnel dashboards and (b) actionable via docs/quickstarts and Console deep links.
- Support/SRE feedback indicates a large % of early churn is tied to avoidable production incidents: wrong key environment (401), rate limit surprises (429), retry storms/timeouts, and streaming disconnect handling.

Non-goals (Phase 1)
- Dedicated/Private production definitions.
- Full compliance/security posture checklist (SOC2/ISO-style). We will include minimal security hygiene only where it prevents common incidents.
- Automated validation of every “production-ready” item. We will define what’s required, and separately define what can be auto-validated vs self-attested.

Proposed definition (Phase 1: Hosted API)
A project is considered to have completed its “first production launch” when ALL of the following are true:
1) Customer has created and used a “prod-mode” API key for a non-trivial workload.
2) Customer has made successful requests from a non-local environment (i.e., not only from Console sample runner), with retries/timeouts configured (SDK defaults acceptable).
3) Customer has configured a minimal set of operational guardrails: rate limit awareness + 429 handling, basic usage/latency visibility, and a rollback/fallback plan (documented).
4) Customer has observed usage in Console (or via API/export) after launch.

Notes:
- “Non-trivial workload” for measurement = ≥ 50 successful requests OR ≥ 250k tokens generated (whichever comes first) within a 24h window after first prod key use. (We may tune thresholds after beta; see Open Questions.)
- “Rollback/fallback plan” in Phase 1 is documentation + recommended implementation approach. We will not require implementing multi-model fallback for GA, but we will require that the customer understands and can execute a rollback path.

Minimum checklist steps (v1)
We will present steps in the Console checklist grouped into two sections: “Get your first success” and “Launch to production.” The production definition is specifically tied to completion of the “Launch to production” section.

A) Get your first success (foundational; not sufficient for production)
A1. Create API key (test)
- What it means: test-mode key created.
- Validation: Console event on key creation.
- Rationale: required to make any request.

A2. Make first successful request
- What it means: at least one 2xx response from the Hosted API for the project.
- Validation: backend validator via gateway logs/metrics (ENG-23113).
- Support-driven rationale: reduces “setup but never called” drop-off.

A3. Optional: Try streaming (recommended but not required)
- What it means: successful streaming session with at least one streamed token.
- Validation: streaming-session detector (ENG-23114).
- Rationale: streaming is a common production mode; but we do not want to block production on it.

B) Launch to production (minimum “first production launch” requirements)
B1. Create API key (prod) + label environment
- Required.
- What it means: prod-mode key created (or existing key explicitly marked as prod) and used at least once.
- Validation: key metadata + first use of prod key (ENG-23117).
- Support rationale: addresses recurring 401 issues from using wrong env key (see SUP-9244).

B2. Configure retries + timeouts (or accept SDK defaults)
- Required.
- What it means: the integration is using either (a) Redwood SDK with default retry/backoff + timeouts enabled, or (b) custom client that implements our recommended policy.
- Validation (Phase 1): self-attested toggle in checklist + docs link; optional heuristic validation via request headers (“x-rw-client”) for SDK usage.
- Required policy (docs canonical):
  - timeouts enabled (connect + read)
  - retry on 429/5xx and network errors with exponential backoff + jitter
  - max retries capped (avoid retry storms)
  - idempotency guidance documented for non-idempotent flows
- Rationale: top production incident driver; also reduces support load.

B3. Understand rate limits/quotas + handle 429
- Required.
- What it means: developer has visited quota/rate limit doc + understands response headers + implements 429 handling.
- Validation: “rate limit education” step click-through + visited quota settings page (ENG-23116 + ENG-23115).
- Support rationale: 429 confusion during onboarding is a major source of tickets (see SUP-9182).

B4. Enable minimal observability
- Required.
- What it means: developer can answer, “Is my app working right now?” and “What is it costing?”
- Minimum requirements:
  - access to usage dashboard for the project (tokens, requests, errors)
  - ability to correlate failures (request id / trace id guidance)
- Validation: “visited usage dashboard” event (ENG-23115). We’ll also include doc links for request IDs.
- SRE rationale: without basic observability, production issues become long, support-heavy threads.

B5. Safe rollout plan (canary/gradual exposure)
- Required.
- What it means: developer acknowledges a recommended rollout sequence (e.g., internal users → small % → ramp) and understands rollback steps.
- Validation (Phase 1): self-attested checklist step; doc deep link to “First production launch” page.
- Rationale: prevents “day 1” saturation and makes failures bounded.

B6. Validate post-launch
- Required.
- What it means: developer observes real production usage after prod key use and confirms expected latencies/error rates.
- Validation: either (a) usage dashboard visit after prod-key first-use OR (b) ≥ X successful prod requests in 24h.
- Rationale: ties “production launch” to an actual, measurable deployment, not just reading docs.

Explicitly NOT required (but recommended) in v1
- Tool calling / structured output usage.
- Multi-region failover.
- Automated evals / prompt regression testing.
- Dedicated alerting setup (PagerDuty, Slack alerts) — recommended for teams with on-call, but not required for self-serve v1.

Copy guidance for the checklist
- Use “Project” consistently (not org/workspace).
- Avoid “SLA/SLO” jargon; use “reliability” and “alerts” in recommended sections.
- Each required step must answer: “Why am I doing this?” in 1–2 lines.

Telemetry + measurement notes
We need to measure:
- Completion funnel to “first production launch” (strict definition) and time-to-complete.
- Drop-off per step.
- Correlation: completion → week-1 retention and token usage growth.

Event requirements for this definition:
- prod key created + prod key first use timestamp
- first successful request timestamp
- usage dashboard visit timestamp
- “retries/timeouts configured” self-attest (boolean) + method (sdk/custom)
- “safe rollout acknowledged” self-attest

Links / artifacts
- Authoritative checklist doc (internal): sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/first-production-launch-checklist.json
- PRD context: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/guided-onboarding-checklist-prd-2026-01.json
- Support failures input: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/onboarding-common-failures-and-fixes.json
- Telemetry schema: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/onboarding-telemetry-event-schema-v1.json

Acceptance criteria
- We have a written, reviewed definition of “first production launch” that (a) can be instrumented with v1 telemetry and (b) maps to concrete checklist steps.
- Each required step has an owner for docs content and a canonical deep link.
- Support and SRE sign off that the minimum set would have prevented the top 3 onboarding escalations we’ve seen (401 env mismatch, 429 surprises, retry/timeout misconfig).
- Console checklist can represent required vs recommended steps (even if recommended steps are not gating completion).

Open questions
1) Threshold tuning for “non-trivial workload” (requests vs tokens): what’s the least gameable but still inclusive metric?
2) Should streaming be “recommended” or “required” for production? (Current: recommended.)
3) Do we require a prod key for production in all cases? (Current: yes, to reduce 401s and encourage key hygiene.)
4) How do we message “rollback/fallback” without implying we provide automatic multi-model fallback in Hosted API v1?

comments: 2026-01-10 — Dev Patel (Support lead): +1 on making “prod vs test key” a required step. We see a lot of 401s where customers copy the wrong key into prod env or rotate keys and forget to update. If the checklist can explicitly say “use a prod key in your deployed environment” it will deflect SUP-9244 style tickets. Also recommend we explicitly link to the 401 troubleshooting section and mention that keys are environment-labeled in Console.

2026-01-12 — Priya Shah (Support engineer): For the 429 step, please include that 429s can come from both per-minute request caps and token throughput caps; customers misinterpret it as “service down.” If we can reference response headers + backoff guidance, it would reduce back-and-forth. Suggest step title: “Handle 429 rate limits (backoff + quotas).”

2026-01-14 — Ethan Park (Platform): Agree with required minimal observability being “visit usage dashboard + request IDs.” From an SRE perspective, we should explicitly document that gateway request IDs are needed in support tickets; otherwise we can’t debug. I’d avoid requiring external alerting for v1; it will block small teams.

2026-01-16 — Amara Diallo (API gateway): On validation: we can reliably detect first-success and prod-key first-use from gateway metrics with ~2–5 min lag. Recommend we do NOT gate completion on immediate updates; the UI should message “may take a few minutes to update.”

2026-01-18 — Marissa Cole (PM, Console): We can support “required vs recommended” UI. For self-attested steps, design wants a consistent “I’ve done this” control with a docs deep link and a “why it matters” tooltip. Need final step ordering by Jan 22 for implementation.

2026-01-21 — Elliot Price (Docs): We can publish a canonical “First production launch” page that matches B1–B6 with anchors. Please lock terminology (project, prod key, usage dashboard). Also: for retries/timeouts, we’ll need language that is SDK-agnostic but includes copy-pastable policies. Writers can add short snippets for Python/TS/Go based on Monica’s team’s standard patterns.

2026-01-24 — Monica Patel (SDK Eng): We can treat “SDK defaults” as satisfying retries/timeouts, but we need to ensure all SDKs have consistent defaults and that docs show how to override. We’ll add a header identifying the client (“x-rw-client”) so we can optionally infer SDK usage for the self-attest step later.

2026-02-03 — Nikhil Sharma (assignee): Marking Done. Final definition and required steps aligned with Support + Platform + Console. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-23116 (429 education step) and ENG-23117 (prod-mode key flow). Docs owners have the canonical page and anchors; telemetry will initially rely on prod key use + usage dashboard visit + self-attest for retries/rollout.
